title: Bramble's Big Cool-Down
markdown:
The sun blasted! Elin practically sweated through her science shirt. Today felt like an oven. Then, a weak bark. Bramble! Her heart leaped. The little seal pup lay like a sun-baked rug. His fur was stuck, his breathing tiny puffs. He looked cooked! Seals sometimes got too hot. This was bad. His eyes looked glassy. Panic prickled. Elin grabbed a towel, dashed to the water, soaked it, and draped it over Bramble. His flippers felt like hot stones. Not enough!

Dr. Ada Brook's jeep crunched to a stop. Her sharp eyes locked onto Bramble. "Elin! Serious trouble." She knelt beside the pup. "Gums pale, flippers like hot stones. He’s trying to pump blood to the surface to lose heat, but his body’s like an engine overheating. Circulation's key, but if it can't dump heat, it's a losing battle."

Dr. Brook watched Bramble's labored breathing. "His kidneys struggle, flushing toxins. His lungs gasp, but breathing hot air won't cool him! We don't sweat like humans. Our cooling comes from evaporation and breathing, vapor pulling heat away. He needs rapid cooling, fast!"

Elin's quick mind sparked. Evaporation! Water turning to vapor pulls heat. "The station's misting system!" she blurted. "Super fine spray! Tons of droplets!"

"Brilliant!" Dr. Brook exclaimed. "And keep him hydrated! Fresh water for those kidneys!"

They dashed to the station. Elin adjusted nozzles to a whisper-fine mist. Dr. Brook guided Bramble onto a cool tarp. The fog settled on him like a blessing. Slowly, Bramble’s panting lessened. His body shuddered, a tremor of relief.

"He's responding!" Elin shouted, excitement bubbling.

Dr. Brook watched Bramble’s breathing deepen. "Yes! The mist evaporates, pulling heat away. It’s like his body’s sweating, but faster." She stroked his head. "Evaporative cooling, Elin. Water changing to vapor takes energy—heat energy—pulling it from Bramble’s body."

Bramble blinked, his obsidian eyes focusing. He managed a weak tail flick.

"See?" Dr. Brook smiled, a brilliant beam. "His body systems—circulation, breathing, kidneys—kicked in once we boosted the cooler, evaporation. It’s a finely tuned machine!" She looked at Elin. "Your quick thinking saved him. You applied what you learned!"

Elin grinned, her chest buzzing. Bramble was going to be okay! The heat suddenly felt less like a threat and more like a challenge. "Today," Elin declared, "was a spectacular success!" And with a happy sigh, she knew her adventures studying the amazing ocean were just beginning!
characters: Elin the marine science student, Bramble the seal pup, Dr. Ada Brook
